title: Custom dashboards, widget types, dashboard templates and reports in the admin portal

prose.label: Reports.
prose.text: {{reports-list}} {{reports-formats-api}} {{reports-create}} Report schedules and the export API are covered in [[portfolio.secops-platform]]; the dashboard schedule details and the API contract are open {{gap:export-schedule-details}}.

measure-dimension-model.statement: Reports, dashboards and saved views use measurements and dimensions: a dimension defines how data is grouped and a measurement the value calculated and displayed; dimensions are grouped by Main Entity and the measurement list follows the selected dimension.

quotes: The dimension defines how data is grouped (e.g., by user, tenant, or severity, etc.) and the measurement defines the value to be calculated and displayed
uses measurements and dimensions to organize and analyze data in reports, dashboards, and saved views
Dimensions are grouped by Main Entity (e.g., Ticket, Asset, etc.), and based on the selected dimension, the measurement list appears.

widget-limits-bar-line-pie.statement: Per widget type the required counts of dimensions and measurements are: bar 1 to 2 dimensions and 1 to 5 measurements; line 1 dimension (a date breakdown counts as one) and 1 to 5 measurements; pie 0 to 1 dimensions and 1 measurement.

quotes: | Bar | 1 to 2 | 1 to 5 | Comparative analysis across dimensions |
| Line | 1 | 1 to 5 | Time-based trends and progression |
| Pie | 0 to 1 | 1 | Proportional distribution of data |
The Date Breakdown setting in historical data (i.e., Day, Week, Month) is not mandatory, but counts as a dimension.

widget-limits-table-tile.statement: A standard table has no limit on dimensions or measurements, a pivot table takes one row dimension, one column dimension and 0 to 5 measurements, and tile and trend widgets take no dimensions and exactly one measurement.

quotes: | Table | No limit | No limit | Detailed tabular data |
| Pivot Table | 1 row dimension 1 column dimension | 0 to 5 | Detailed tabular data |
| Tile and Trend | 0 | 1 | Highlighting single metrics or KPIs |

widget-variants.statement: Bar widgets come as vertical or horizontal, stacked and 100% stacked; line widgets as line or spline; pie widgets as pie or donut; table widgets as standard or pivot; any widget type can be previewed as a table; trend widgets are only available with historical data.

quotes: Vertical and horizontal 100% stacked bars
Spline charts (smooth continuous curves)
Donut chart
Pivot table
all other widget types can be previewed as a table by enabling Table View
Trend widgets are only available when displaying historical data.
Vertical and horizontal bars
Vertical and horizontal stacked bars
Line charts (straight segments)
Pie chart (standard)
Table (standard)

dashboard-access.statement: A custom dashboard needs at least one widget; Viewers and Editors can each be Public (all users in the account) or specific users, leaving the Viewers or Editors drop-down blank keeps the dashboard private, edit access overrides view access, and dashboards can be tagged and pinned to apps.

quotes: You must add at least one widget to configure a new custom dashboard.
Public: Select to grant view access to all users in the account.
To keep the dashboard private, leave the Viewers drop-down menu blank.
The edit access overrides the view access.
Pin to Apps: (Optional) Select the application that you want to pin to the dashboard.
Public: Select to grant edit access to all users in the account.
You can add one or more tags to a dashboard to categorize it.
To keep the dashboard private, leave the Editors drop-down menu blank.

dashboard-templates.statement: Dashboards can start from preconfigured templates on the Template Gallery page (edited and saved as new, or duplicated) that can be customized; separately, the Create New Dashboard window offers Import Template to upload a dashboard template.

quotes: using preconfigured dashboard templates from the Template Gallery page
These templates include preconfigured widgets designed to address common use cases that you can customize as necessary.
You can also clone an existing template to create a new dashboard.
Click Save As.
In the Create New Dashboard window:
You can also click Import Template to upload a dashboard template.

dashboard-pinning.statement: A dashboard pinned to an app appears on that app's My Dashboards page.

quotes: Pinned dashboards are listed on the app's My Dashboards page.

dashboards-page.statement: The dashboards list (Explore > Dashboards) shows creator, sharing settings, the apps a dashboard is shared to, tags, last update and scheduled-export status, supports activating and deactivating scheduled exports, sending an export email, and bulk tag editing that either adds to or replaces existing tags.

quotes: Activate scheduled exports for a dashboard.
Send a dashboard export email to the configured recipients.
Add to existing tags: Add new tags to the dashboard along with the existing tags.
Replace existing tags: Replace the existing tags with new tags.
Scheduled Export: The status of the dashboard export schedule (Active or Inactive).
Deactivate scheduled exports for a dashboard.
Created By: The name of the user who created the dashboard.
Sharing Settings: The names of the users who can edit or view the dashboard (e.g., Public or specific users).
Apps: The applications to which the dashboard is shared.
Tags: The tags assigned to the dashboard.
Last Updated: The date and time when the dashboard was last updated.

widget-actions.statement: A dashboard widget can be edited, shown as a table, expanded to full screen, duplicated with the same measurements, dimensions, filters and visualization settings, set to scroll, exported to CSV, deleted, resized and rearranged.

quotes: Full Screen: Click the More Options icon, and click Full Screen to expand the widget.
The duplicate widget uses the same measurements, dimensions, filters, and visualization settings.
Enable Scrolling: Click the More Options icon, and click Enable Scrolling to make the widget scrollable when it contains more data than can fit in the widget area on a dashboard.
Export As CSV: Click the More Options icon, and click Export As CSV to download the widget data to a CSV file.
Edit Widget: Click the Edit Widget icon to modify the displayed data or update the widget configuration.
Table View: Click the Table View icon to display the widget data in a table.
Delete: Click the More Options icon, and click Delete to remove the widget from the dashboard.
Drag the corner of a widget to resize it.
Drag and drop a widget to rearrange its order or location on the dashboard.

reports-list.statement: The Reports page (Explore > Reports) lists each report's ID, app, creator, sharing status, last run time in UTC, last updater and scheduled export details (frequency, format and destination), and reports can be activated, deactivated, rerun, duplicated and tagged.

quotes: Last Run Time (UTC): The date and time the report was last run, displayed in UTC.
Schedule Export Details: The schedule details for exporting the report, including the frequency, format, and delivery destination.
Rerun a selected report.
ID: The unique identifier of the report.
App: The application the report belongs to.
Created By: The user who created the report.
Sharing Settings: The sharing status of the reports (e.g., Private, Public, or shared with specific users).
Updated By: The user who last updated the report.
Activate a selected report.
Deactivate a selected report.
Duplicate a selected report.
Edit tags for a selected report.

reports-formats-api.statement: Reports can be delivered on a schedule and exported in CSV, JSONL or Excel format, and exports can be triggered programmatically via an API.

quotes: Schedule automated delivery and export data in CSV, JSONL, or Excel format.
Trigger report exports programmatically via an API.

reports-create.statement: A report has Viewers and Editors (Public or selected users, edit overriding view), a Current or History data type with a preconfigured, custom or dynamic date range for history, and can be saved with Done, Save, Save & Run or Save As New; it can also be opened from My Reports under Vulnerabilities, Assets, Identities and SOC Workbench.

quotes: Select this option to grant view access to all users in the account.
The edit access overrides the view access.
set the date filter to either Current or History.
You can select a preconfigured range, create a custom range, or set a dynamic range.
Select Save & Run from the Save drop-down menu to save the report and immediately apply export settings, if configured.
SOC Workbench > My Reports
For historical reports, click the date filter to specify the desired date range.
Vulnerabilities > My Reports
Assets > My Reports
Identities > My Reports
Click Done to save and close the report, redirecting you to the Reports page.
Click Save to save the report. If scheduled, the report exports at the set time.
Select Save As New from the Save drop-down menu to save your changes as a new report.
Public: Select this option to grant view access to all users in the account.
Selected Users: Select specific users to set them as viewers.
Editors: Select the users who can edit the report.
Public: Select to grant edit access to all users in the account.
Selected Users: Select specific users that can edit the report.

line-example-dimensions.title: Does a line widget with a month breakdown and a Severity series fit the 1-dimension limit?
line-example-dimensions.detail: The widget types page lists line widgets at 'Dimensions: 1' with the date breakdown counting as a dimension, but its example shows time broken down by month with each line a severity level, which reads as two dimensions. The page does not reconcile the two.

export-schedule-details.title: Dashboard export schedule details and the report export API contract
export-schedule-details.detail: The dashboards page names the export schedule only as a status column. Report schedule destinations and frequencies are in portfolio.secops-platform:report-schedule and the Reporting API basics in portfolio.secops-platform:reporting-api; what remains open is the dashboard schedule configuration and the API request contract.
